record.context_brief: Betti-number bounds in almost or nearly Gorenstein families
record.original_question: If Gamma is an almost symmetric or nearly Gorenstein numerical semigroup, are there upper bounds for the Betti numbers b_i(R_Gamma) of its local semigroup ring R_Gamma that depend only on the embedding dimension edim(Gamma)?

evidence.quote: Problem 22 ([S18, Question 3.7]). Let Γ be an almost symmetric or nearly Gorenstein numerical semigroup. Are there upper bounds for the Betti numbers bi(RΓ ) in terms of edim(Γ )?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Gamma \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ be a numerical semigroup, i.e., a cofinite submonoid of $(\mathbb{N},+)$ containing $0$. Let $g_1 < g_2 < \cdots < g_e$ be its minimal system of generators, so the embedding dimension is $\mathrm{edim}(\Gamma)=e$. Fix a field $k$ and consider the local semigroup ring 
$$R_\Gamma = k[[t^{g_1},\ldots,t^{g_e}]] \subseteq k[[t]],$$
with maximal ideal $\mathfrak{m}=(t^{g_1},\ldots,t^{g_e})$. Denote by $b_i(R_\Gamma)=\dim_k \mathrm{Tor}_i^{R_\Gamma}(k,k)$ the $i$-th Betti number of $R_\Gamma$ (equivalently, the $i$-th Betti number in the minimal free resolution of $k$ as an $R_\Gamma$-module, or of $R_\Gamma$ over the regular ambient ring $k[[x_1,\ldots,x_e]]$ via the surjection $x_j\mapsto t^{g_j}$).

Recall the Apéry set $\mathrm{Ap}(\Gamma,g_1)=\{w\in\Gamma : w-g_1\notin\Gamma\}$, the Frobenius number $F(\Gamma)=\max(\mathbb{Z}\setminus\Gamma)$, and the set of pseudo-Frobenius numbers $\mathrm{PF}(\Gamma)=\{x\in\mathbb{Z}\setminus\Gamma : x+\Gamma\setminus\{0\}\subseteq\Gamma\}$. The semigroup $\Gamma$ is called:
\begin{itemize}
\item \emph{almost symmetric} if for every $x\in\mathrm{PF}(\Gamma)\setminus\{F(\Gamma)\}$ one has $F(\Gamma)-x\in\mathrm{PF}(\Gamma)$;
\item \emph{nearly Gorenstein} if the trace ideal $\mathrm{tr}(\omega_{R_\Gamma})$ of the canonical module $\omega_{R_\Gamma}$ contains the maximal ideal $\mathfrak{m}$.
\end{itemize}

Question: For each $i\geq 0$, does there exist a function $C_i:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ such that 
$$b_i(R_\Gamma)\leq C_i(\mathrm{edim}(\Gamma))$$
holds for every numerical semigroup $\Gamma$ that is almost symmetric, and likewise for every numerical semigroup $\Gamma$ that is nearly Gorenstein?
artifact.status_search_result: The general question is largely open. Partial results are known: for nearly Gorenstein numerical semigroups of embedding dimension 4 the Cohen–Macaulay type is at most 3, and for embedding dimension 5 the type is bounded (at most 40 if not almost symmetric). Bounds on all Betti numbers in terms of embedding dimension remain an active research topic with no general proof known.

status_evidence.title: Nearly Gorenstein and almost symmetric properties in shifted numerical semigroups
status_evidence.snippet: The type of nearly Gorenstein numerical semigroups minimally generated by 5 integers is bounded; if not almost symmetric, the type is at most 40. In embedding dimension four, the Cohen–Macaulay type is at most three.
status_evidence.claim: Partial bounds on the first Betti number (the type) are known in low embedding dimensions for nearly Gorenstein semigroups, but the general bound on all $b_i$ remains open.

status_evidence.title: Betti numbers for numerical semigroup rings
status_evidence.snippet: Question on whether there is any bound for the type and the remaining Betti numbers of k[H] in terms of embedding dimension when H is almost or nearly Gorenstein.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is explicitly posed as an open question in the literature on Betti numbers of numerical semigroup rings.
